world.summary: The world fixes hold. All five seam sites from verify-world-01 (tour f711, f555, f815, f45, f305) now match 82bab12 in the amplified difference, apart from the wave's intended ground change. Mesh clipping calmed the old z-fights a lot: changed pixels per held frame at street_skyline_up (f275) fell from 3.88 to 0.21 per mille, at a2_doors (f67) from 1.81 to 0.31 and at the warehouse (f171) from 0.97 to 0.17. No pose flickers more than before. I found no hole, crack, texture jump or shading break at any cut. The boss roof gap stays fixed: tour pose 17 is 0.02 per mille against 0.31 on 82bab12, and ground_flicker gives the same digits as d582d21 for all 14 drift phases. The rooms show no visible change against d582d21 at any of the 10 poses, and their temporal numbers are identical. The one world cost is cosmetic: the solver's 'bigger box wins' rule now draws the wall over trim that showed at 82bab12 (a warehouse jamb, a door reveal, two pilaster edge strips). verify-world-02 is fixed: looking down 45 degrees, behind lights the bottom, left the left and front the top. The rear jab is now as plain as the front one (94/89/71% of the bottom band changed at +2/+4/+8 frames, against 58/72/69% for the top on a front jab; it was 71/63/43% at d582d21). The real hits in passive_six land on the attacker's side. The fix pass did break one thing in the hurt cue. hurt_overlay_bottom_ink_gain lets the stored bottom edge strength go above 1, and that value feeds the depth carry-over `_depth * _alive_share()`. So every clean rear hit of about 7 damage or more multiplies the vignette depth, with no upper limit and no reset. A probe test shows rear 20-damage hits 2 s apart give depths of 0.32, 0.48, 0.72, 1.08, 1.62 and 2.43 of the screen height (the limit is 0.32). In the hurt act, a Bruiser smash from behind (f2189) raises the bottom strokes to about 63% of the screen height, past the crosshair. The same frame at d582d21 reaches about 33%.

code.summary: Code-lens review of the fix pass, 3e7084e against d582d21. I found one real regression introduced by the pass (medium) and six low ledger, rule and robustness items. Everything else the brief asked about checked out. The regression is the hurt overlay's vignette depth, which compounds by about 1.5x per heavy hit from behind and never decays; I measured it with a temporary test, now deleted. Fixes confirmed: the floor-plane hit_bearing (restoring the old function makes 11 of the new tests fail), the Kicker's eyes config with a pinning test, the strain ratchet back at 2afbe4d's figures except one logged row, and the clipped-mesh solver, scan and guards. Clipping is correct (winding, UV, normal, colour carried) and the collider is untouched. I did not re-run the full suite or look at any image.
checked: hit_bearing: put d582d21's function back in the review worktree and ran tests/test_m6_feedback_feel.gd. Failures: the behind-at-45, behind-at-60, front-at-30-up, left, right and carried-roll jab tests, plus the pitch/roll bearing test (pitch -80 and others). Restored: 42/42 pass.
view_transform() is `return _view` (reads state only). HurtOverlay falls back to camera.global_transform for a non-FirstPersonCamera and to the victim's transform with no camera.

hit_bearing edge cases: attacker null, freed or outside the tree and within hurt_bearing_min_m both fall back to -direction in the yaw frame. Straight above or below the lens gives a near-zero floor vector and takes the same fallback. Pitch is clamped to 89 degrees and the KO view uses 85 degrees, so get_euler yaw is stable; the test covers pitch -80 with roll.

Solver: stripped every yields_to from the three scenes in the review worktree and ran tools/solve_insets.tscn. It produced 97 YIELD lines and 0 UNSOLVED, identical as a set to the 97 yields in the committed scenes. It ran in this one session; the order is sorted and the rule is a fixed total order. Scenes restored with git checkout.
apply_yields.py: read it; it writes only yields_to lines and the script ExtResource of nodes under Geometry, and drops the ext_resource if unused.

MeshClip: kit meshes carry exactly vertex, normal, uv, color and index (KitMesh), and all are carried through. Probe on 9 kinds with two rects on all six faces: 0 flipped triangles before and after (winding kept), strip id (colour alpha) constant per triangle, UV interpolated. T-junctions exist along cut seams but are positioned by lerp to within about 1e-7 m. I saw no crack evidence in code or in the lead's difference images, and did not render for it. Degenerate tris: about 107 zero-area fan triangles in the level, harmless.
Collider: tests/test_m6_colliders.gd 3/3 pass; clipping only replaces the mesh.

yields_to robustness: renamed a target block in street.tscn (LeftWall to LeftWallX). The silent skip brought the z-fight back and test_no_two_drawn_faces_of_the_level fails (22/23 passed). The failure is loud in the test only, not at runtime. A mutual yield makes holes() fire, covered by an existing test.

Cross-section yield: boss_roof EntryFenceR to Roofs CurbEast. Sections are never unloaded (no queue_free in level_root or level_section). Built alone, the path resolves to null and the block draws fully (z-fight at most, no hole).

RoomKit.resolve_coplanar: called at the end of crowd_room._build_geometry and in test_room._ready; deterministic (volume, then earlier index, a total order); idempotent. Instancing the crowd and training rooms costs the same as before (about 205 and 78 ms each).
tests/test_m6_feedback_ground.gd: 23/23 pass; test_m6_feedback_detail 19/19, _kicker 10/10, _boss 11/11, test_tuning_panel 28/28.

tuning/default.json: ran `godot --headless -s tools/gen_default_preset.gd`; git shows no diff. The new kit tunables (kit_coplanar_m, kit_clip_standoff_m) and the four hurt tunables (outline width and colour, bottom_ink_gain, bottom_stroke_gain) are @export_range with defaults, in the Level > Ground and Hit-feel groups.

Cost: instantiating mission1.tscn headless (`_initialize` probe, load + add_child + 2 frames). d582d21: 1149 and 1089 ms; 3e7084e: 1509 and 1377 ms, so about +0.3 s once at level load. Unique ArrayMeshes 192 to 253, vertices 58,538 to 63,203, triangles 54,013 to 55,524, static memory 271.3 to 272.5 MB. All sections are instanced at load, so there is no mid-play rebuild; no code assigns size or draw_box on InsetBlocks at runtime.
HurtOverlay.edge_strength readers: only tests and the draw path, which now clamps alpha. The depth bug in finding 1 comes from _alive_share(), which reads the unclamped edges.

Layer rules: the overlay and camera only read state (hit.attacker.global_position, view_transform()). Diff grep for api key, secret or token found nothing real; no tools/pipeline changes; no Tripo, Gemini or ElevenLabs call in the diff.

Numbers in scripts: found `const MIN_AREA_M2` in mesh_clip.gd and `maxf(color.a, 0.01)` in hurt_overlay.gd (reported in finding 7). No other new const in inset_block, room_kit, hurt_overlay or the camera beyond the meta key CLIPPED_META.

also_noticed: held.min was loosened 22% (0.1489 to 0.1168), well past the ratchet's usual margin. It is logged with a reason (colour borders move the decimation), but I did not verify why a palette change moves mesh strain. Nobody looked at whether the stiff idle's squash pinches visibly.
About 107 zero-area fan triangles come out of MeshClip in the level (collinear fan points). They cost nothing at raster time; dropping triangles under 1e-9 m2 would tidy the mesh.
InsetBlock `_clips()` runs only when the block builds, so a block moved at runtime would keep stale cuts. Nothing moves them today.
The scan's COPLANAR_M (0.004) duplicates Tuning kit_coplanar_m instead of reading it, so tuning the preset would let the scan and the build disagree.

Sibling-order dependency: a block that yields to a Dressing piece only clips if the piece's mesh is already built when the block's _ready runs. That holds today (the scan passes at 0.0001 m2), but reordering the Dressing after the Geometry in a section would bring the z-fights back, caught only by the scan test.

findings.title: Kicker at 1-1.2 m: a pale skin strip under the brim, over a cap-black bar, sits between the brim and the new shade, so the front reads brim / skin / dark bar / brown / mask
findings.detail: The fix pass made the eyes band a brown shade (slot 24, z 1.625-1.665) and kept the cap-black faces just above it (the 149 faces the test pins). Above those, though, are slot-6 skin faces at z 1.66-1.70 (y up to 0.145), behind the brim's front (y 0.168). At 1 m and 1.2 m they show as a pale crescent under the brim, and the slot-23 faces at z 1.66-1.67 below it read as a dark bar across the eyes. The result is a skin strip boxed in by dark above and below, which the concept does not have: kicker_c.jpg puts the brim directly over the shaded eyes. At 20% health the strip bleeds red under the brim, a forehead visibly bleeding under a cap. The strip is pre-existing: it is in 82bab12 and d582d21 too. In d582d21 it blended into the pale band below it; now it stands out against the brown shade. It is gone by 2.5 m.

findings.title: The bottom ink gain makes the hurt vignette's depth ratchet: each clean rear hit of about 7 damage or more multiplies it, with no limit and no reset
findings.detail: VFIX-FEEL stores the bottom edge as weight x strength x hurt_overlay_bottom_ink_gain (1.5), so edge_strength(BOTTOM) reaches 1.5. on_player_hit then sets _depth = max(_depth * _alive_share(), base), where _alive_share() = max(_edges) and is read AFTER the new hit is stored. Before this pass that factor was at most 1, so the depth never exceeded hurt_overlay_depth_max. Now any rear hit with strength x 1.5 > 1 multiplies the previous depth by up to 1.5. That takes strength above 0.67, about 7 damage: the Kicker's 8, the Thug's pipe 10, the Bruiser's smash 15, Ox's 15-25. _depth never decays (only the edges do), so the growth also carries across hits seconds apart. The depth sets both the vignette's reach and the strokes' length on every edge. Game-boy would see it in a fight: in the hurt act, the Bruiser smash from behind at f2186 follows the left and right smashes. Its bottom strokes rise to about 63% of the screen height, past the crosshair and over the THUD, where d582d21 reached about 33% at the same frame. The third pipe hit from behind (f3751) reaches about 40-45%, against about 25% before. In a boss fight, two or three rear hits push the vignette over the whole screen. That is the heavy, view-blocking run of hits the brief asked to avoid.
findings.evidence: Probe GUT test on 3e7084e (output /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-arachne-repos-beat-em-up-PoC/21dfb0ac-e45b-4ac0-bc13-2a0a12b0eada/scratchpad/probe.out), depth_share after each hit, with depth_max 0.32: rear 20 damage, hits 2.0 s apart: 0.320 0.480 0.720 1.080 1.620 2.430; rear 20 damage, 0.25 s apart: the same; rear 10 damage: 0.220 to 0.396 over 6 hits; rear 8 damage: 0.200 to 0.255; rear 5 damage: flat 0.170; front 20 damage: flat 0.320. Code: game/ui/hurt_overlay.gd:110-112 (the ink gain stored in _edges), :121-122 (_depth * _alive_share()), :142-143 (_alive_share = max(_edges.max(), _strokes.max())). Frames: captures/m6-verify-final/hurt/bot.avi f2189 and f3751 against captures/m6-feedback-verify/hurt/bot.avi at the same frames (scratchpad hurt_ba.png); f1406 (front smash, top teeth about 29%) against f2189 (hurt4.png)
findings.repro: Add a test to tests/test_m6_feedback_feel.gd: HurtOverlay.new(); land HitInfo(damage 20, direction (0,0,-1)) with Transform3D.IDENTITY three times, with advance(2.0) between hits; assert depth_share() <= Tuning.data.hurt_overlay_depth_max. It fails today (0.72 after the third hit). Or watch 'Look: player hurt' at the 'bruiser smash behind' beat (f2186-2200).
findings.suggested_fix: In game/ui/hurt_overlay.gd, keep the stored _edges at 1 or below and apply hurt_overlay_bottom_ink_gain only when drawing: in _draw, pass strength * gain to _draw_vignette for the bottom edge of a clean hit, with the alpha clamp already there. Or at least clamp _alive_share() to 1 (minf(maxf(_edges.max(), _strokes.max()), 1.0)) and clamp _depth to hurt_overlay_depth_max. Then add the test above, a run of three rear Thug pipe hits whose depth stays at most depth_max, and re-record the hurt act.

votes.reason: The code path is as described. A clean rear hit stores edge[BOTTOM] = weight x strength x 1.5, which can exceed 1. on_player_hit then computes _depth = max(_depth * _alive_share(), base). _alive_share() is max(_edges, _strokes) read after the new hit is stored, so the factor can reach 1.5. _depth is only ever set in on_player_hit and never decays or resets, so the growth is unbounded across hits and persists after the edges fade.
votes.evidence: game/ui/hurt_overlay.gd lines 110-112 (ink gain applied to the stored _edges), 121-122 (_depth * _alive_share()), 142-143 (_alive_share is a bare max with no clamp), 151 (depth_px = _depth * size.y). tuning_data.gd:286 sets hurt_overlay_bottom_ink_gain to 1.5 and :228 sets depth_max to 0.32. The 3e7084e diff against d582d21 adds the ink multiplier. That multiplier is what lifts the factor above 1, since before it _edges and _strokes were at most 1. I did not rerun the probe. The reviewer's reported output (depth 0.32, 0.48, 0.72, 1.08 for 20-damage rear hits) matches the arithmetic: 0.32 x 1.5 per hit.
votes.root_cause: The bottom-edge ink gain is baked into the stored _edges values, which also serve as the decay-share multiplier for _depth. _alive_share() is therefore no longer bounded by 1, so the max(_depth * share, base) line in on_player_hit grows geometrically. _depth is never clamped to hurt_overlay_depth_max and never decays.

findings.title: The bottom stroke gain scales the whole depth, so a full-damage rear hit's teeth reach about 56% of the screen height even without the ratchet
findings.detail: _draw uses reach = depth_px * hurt_overlay_bottom_stroke_gain (1.4), and a tooth's length goes up to depth x (stroke_len_min + stroke_len_range) = 1.25 x depth. The depth already grows with damage (0.12 to 0.32), so the gain meant to lift the teeth clear of the HP panel makes a heavy rear hit's teeth up to 1.75 x 0.32 = 0.56 of the screen height, across its centre. A light jab needs the lift (about 0.30 of the height); a heavy hit does not. Fixing the ratchet above removes most of what f2189 shows, but this proportional part remains.
findings.evidence: game/ui/hurt_overlay.gd:157-158 (reach = depth_px * hurt_overlay_bottom_stroke_gain), :217-218 (tooth length = depth x (0.55 + rand x 0.7) x clamp(strength + 0.3)); tuning_data.gd hurt_overlay_depth_max 0.32, stroke_len_min 0.55, stroke_len_range 0.7; hurt f2189 teeth tips at about y 330 of 900 (scratchpad hurt_ba.png, top right)
findings.repro: After clamping the ratchet, land one 20-damage clean hit from behind with the overlay at 1600x900 and measure the longest bottom tooth: about 0.56 of the height, against about 0.40 for the same hit from the front.
findings.suggested_fix: Lift the bottom teeth by a fixed amount instead of a factor, for example reach = depth_px + hurt_overlay_bottom_lift x size.y, with the lift set to the HP panel's height. Or cap reach at hurt_overlay_depth_max x size.y x gain. Put the number in Hit feel > Hurt.

findings.title: The hurt vignette's depth compounds 1.5x per heavy hit from behind and never decays (bottom_ink_gain regression)
findings.detail: The pass lets the bottom edge's strength reach 1.5 (hurt_overlay_bottom_ink_gain) but HurtOverlay.on_player_hit still sets `_depth = maxf(_depth * _alive_share(), ...)`, and _alive_share() is `maxf(_edges.max(), _strokes.max())` (about line 144), which was at most 1 before and now exceeds 1. `_depth` is never reduced in advance(), so every clean hit from behind with strength above about 0.667 (damage above about 6.7) multiplies the stored depth by 1.5 times strength. Hits from the sides or front multiply it by 1 or less, so only behind hits grow it. A full-strength behind hit therefore grows the depth by 1.5x each time (the Bruiser smash, 20+ damage) and a 10-damage one by about 1.1x. The depth is shared by all four edges and the bottom strokes (reach times 1.4), so after a few rear blows the ink vignette covers most or all of the screen and stays that way until side hits shrink it. This is the one thing the ask to feel the hits you take could regress, and the single-hit look acts and tests cannot see it.
findings.evidence: Temporary test (tests/test_zz_review_depth.gd, since deleted) calling HurtOverlay.on_player_hit(hit from Vector3.BACK, damage) repeatedly with advance(2.0) between hits. Depth after each of 6 hits: damage 20 gives 0.320, 0.480, 0.720, 1.080, 1.620, 2.430 (hurt_overlay_depth_max is 0.32); damage 10 gives 0.220, 0.247, 0.278, 0.313, 0.352, 0.396; damage 6 stays 0.180. The same hits from Vector3.LEFT stay flat at 0.320 and 0.220. Code: game/ui/hurt_overlay.gd:121 and :144; the gain at :112.
findings.repro: In a GUT test: `var o := HurtOverlay.new(); add_child_autofree(o)`, then 4 times `o.on_player_hit(hit, Transform3D.IDENTITY)` with hit.direction = Vector3.FORWARD (hit from behind), hit.damage = 20, hit.attacker = null, calling o.advance(2.0) between hits, then read o.depth_share() (1.08 by the 4th hit, against a 0.32 tunable maximum). In play: let a Bruiser smash you from behind 3 or more times.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the share at most 1: `_depth = maxf(_depth * minf(_alive_share(), 1.0), ...)`, or compute _alive_share() from the edges before the bottom gain is applied. Clamp _depth to hurt_overlay_depth_max as well. Add a test that N behind hits at full damage leave depth_share() at most hurt_overlay_depth_max.

votes.reason: Confirmed by code reading: the depth grows without bound on repeated strong hits from behind. I did not run the repro test.
votes.evidence: In game/ui/hurt_overlay.gd, on_player_hit sets _edges[BOTTOM] = max(.., weights*strength*ink) with ink = hurt_overlay_bottom_ink_gain = 1.5 (tuning_data.gd:286), before line 121 runs. Line 121 then does _depth = maxf(_depth * _alive_share(), ...), and _alive_share() (line 144) returns the max of the edges and strokes, which now reaches 1.5. For a full-damage hit from dead behind the bottom weight is about 1, so the edge is 1.5 and _depth is multiplied by 1.5 each hit. advance() (lines 47-54) fades only _edges and _strokes, never _depth. The fresh edges are written before _alive_share() is read, so fading between hits does not stop the growth. The only floor on the new depth is lerp(min, max, damage_share), capped at hurt_overlay_depth_max (0.32), and that floor is a lower bound, not a ceiling. Nothing clamps _depth. The reviewer's reported figures (0.32, 0.48, 0.72, 1.08, ...) match this arithmetic.
votes.root_cause: _alive_share() was meant to return a 0..1 fade share, but it now includes the 1.5x bottom ink gain. Using it as a multiplier on the stored _depth therefore compounds, and _depth has no decay or clamp.

findings.title: verify-code-06 is not closed: the roll-out closure test still passes on a path in a string that nothing uses
findings.detail: _roll_out_file_problem now needs one `func test_` line and the pipeline path on a line that does not start with `#`. It does not tie the two together. A file with an empty `func test_x(): pass` and an unused `const P := "...characters/<id>/pipeline.json"` passes, and so does a path in a trailing comment after code. The twin test's own last assertion encodes this: it expects a file whose test never reads the constant to pass. The character therefore still stays out of the shared guards without a real roll-out test.
findings.evidence: tests/test_m6_feedback_detail.gd, _roll_out_file_problem (lines 171-186) and the last assertion of test_the_roll_out_closure_rejects_a_bare_string (about line 197).
findings.repro:
Call _roll_out_file_problem("extends GutTest
const P := "res://assets/source/characters/thug/pipeline.json"
func test_a() -> void:
	pass
", "thug") and it returns "". Likewise `pass # characters/thug/pipeline.json`.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the path to appear inside a test function body, or require a call that loads it (FileAccess/load with the path). Strip trailing comments before matching. Also require the file's tests to assert on the loaded config.

findings.title: Clipping leaves orphaned plinth tops and end caps floating where a wall's face is taken out
findings.detail: MeshClip removes only faces whose normal points out of the plane. A tall wall's 5 cm plinth board has a front (removed with the face) plus a top ledge and two end caps (kept). Where a clipped rectangle covers the board, a hollow 5 cm ledge is left standing in front of the partner's face, which has no plinth there. VFIX-WORLD.md knows the ledges stay; the hollow-ledge side effect is new with this pass. It is likely to ink as a short line along the wall foot.
findings.evidence: Probe (captures/review/probe_orphans.gd) counts triangles 3 mm to 7 cm out from a clipped plane inside a clipped rectangle: StartWall 6, EndWall 17, RightWall 5, Terrace/RightAWall0 8 and Catwalk/EndWall0 8 triangles. The sampled ones are normals (0,1,0) and (0,0,+-1) at the wall foot, y -5.8 to -5.4 in the block's frame. Summary line: `clipped blocks 89 with orphan standoff tris 5`.
findings.repro: godot --headless res://captures/review/probe_orphans.tscn --quit-after 2000 in the review worktree, or clip KitMesh.build(&"wall", Vector3(6,4,0.6)) over its whole +z face: 4 triangles remain beyond the plane (top and caps).
findings.suggested_fix: In clip(), also drop standoff-board faces (those with every vertex within depth of the plane) whose centroid projects inside a clipped rectangle, whatever their normal.

findings.title: steps() exempts every `fence` block and everything under a Barrier, which also hides one real step
findings.detail: _stands_by_design() drops any pair with a look-`fence` block or a Barrier descendant. Without it, steps() finds 23 pairs at 0.02 m2 and 118 at 0.0001 m2 in the level. Almost all are rail posts against bars and curbs. One is not: a shutter panel under Barriers/ShutterStair3 stands 40 mm in front of Catwalk/Lintel3's x faces (1.50 m2 covering, 3.00 m2 of the lintel left in view), which the edge pass will ink along the panel's edge. The shutter is arguably by design, but the blanket rule would equally hide a future fence-look wall that steps in front of a wall.
findings.evidence: captures/review/scan_nox.gd (the scan with `_stands_by_design` returning false) via captures/review/probe_scan.tscn: `STEPNO Barriers/ShutterStair3/@MeshInstance3D@476 stands 40 mm in front of Geometry/Catwalk/Lintel3 (x- faces): 1.50 m2 ...`.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the exemption to the pair types that need it (a fence block against its curb or rail partner, a Barrier panel against its own frame), or list the accepted pairs by name.

findings.title: Small rule slips: a numeric const in mesh_clip.gd and a bare epsilon in hurt_overlay.gd
findings.detail: MeshClip has `const MIN_AREA_M2 := 0.0000001`, a geometric epsilon that is not a Tuning value (the code rules say no numbers in scripts). hurt_overlay.gd's rim alpha divides by `maxf(color.a, 0.01)`. The scan's COPLANAR_M (0.004) duplicates the tunable instead of reading it. These are minor and not feel numbers.
findings.evidence: game/level/kit/mesh_clip.gd line 16; game/ui/hurt_overlay.gd, the `rim` line in _draw_strokes; tests/m6_coplanar_scan.gd line 31.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the sliver floor to Tuning (or document it as a numerical epsilon) and read kit_coplanar_m in the scan.
